text: Moses "endured as seeing Him who is invisible." The Greek word means he stayed strong, and at 120 his eyes weren't dim.
explanation:
The verb translated "endured," kartereo, appears only here in the New Testament. It comes from kratos, strength or might. It's less about gritting your teeth and more about staying strong. When Moses died at 120, "his eyes were not dim nor his natural vigour diminished."

The secret: he kept "seeing Him who is invisible." Moses saw Christ in Aaron's budding rod and in the bronze serpent lifted up. You see Him today in His Word. The more you behold Him, the more you're changed into His likeness, and He's forever young and strong at the Father's right hand.

text: "Those who wait on the Lord shall renew their strength": literally exchange it. Your limited strength for His unlimited.
explanation:
"Even the youths shall faint and be weary." Being young is no guarantee; natural strength runs out. The Hebrew for renew, chalaph, means to change or exchange. And to wait, qavah, is to look with expectation; it's the root of tikvah, hope, the name of Israel's national anthem.

So waiting on the Lord isn't sitting idle. It's looking away from everything else to Jesus with hope. As you do, you trade natural strength for His, and "they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint."

text: Psalm 90's "seventy years, or eighty" was written under wrath in the wilderness. The very next psalm says, "With long life I will satisfy him."
explanation:
Many accept seventy or eighty years as God's limit. But read the verses around it: "For all our days have passed away in Your wrath… Who knows the power of Your anger?" It's Moses' psalm about a generation under judgment in the wilderness. Even the law limited the Levites' service to between twenty-five and fifty.

You're not under wrath. After the cross of Isaiah 53, God swore in Isaiah 54 that He would never be angry with you, as surely as He'd never flood the earth again. Moses himself lived to 120 with full strength. Don't let a verse about judgment set the limits of your life under grace.

text: At nearly one hundred, Abraham ran to greet his guests. At ninety, Sarah received strength to conceive.
explanation:
When the Lord appeared by the oaks of Mamre, Abraham "ran from the tent door to meet them," then "hurried into the tent to Sarah" and "ran to the herd." This was a man about a hundred years old. And "by faith Sarah herself also received strength to conceive seed when she was past the age." The word is dunamis, power, and her youth was so renewed that a king wanted her for his harem.

Not through ginseng or anti-ageing creams, but through faith. If you belong to Christ, you're Abraham's seed and heirs of his blessing, and that blessing touched their bodies. Believe God to renew your youth like the eagle's.

text: Behind every fear lies the fear of death. Jesus died to destroy the one who held that power.
explanation:
Jesus took on flesh and blood "that through death He might destroy him who had the power of death, that is, the devil, and release those who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage." Fear of flying, fear of disease, fear of the future: dig deep enough and you'll find it there.

When David felled Goliath, he didn't stop at the stone. He took the giant's own sword and cut off his head. At the cross, Jesus used death itself to defeat the one who wielded it. The devil can't simply call your number. You're free to live without that lifelong bondage.

text: At 93, George Müller said, "I have no aches or pains, no rheumatism." His secret: the recuperative power of God's Word.
explanation:
Müller cared for more than ten thousand orphans by prayer alone, and in his seventies and eighties travelled to forty-two countries as a missionary. In his ninety-third year he wrote that he could still do a day's work at the orphan houses with ease, while younger friends complained of their ailments. Asked his secret, he credited the recuperative power of God's Word on his body.

"My words… are life to those who find them, and health to all their flesh." The Hebrew for health, marpe, can mean medicine. Müller found that beginning each day in the Word, not straining in prayer against wandering thoughts, made his soul happy in the Lord. Then he could face everything else in the right spirit.

text: The Emmaus couple walked seven miles home, heard Jesus open the Scriptures, then walked seven miles back that same night.
explanation:
Jesus restrained their eyes so they wouldn't recognise Him. Why? Because it was more important for them to see Him in the Scriptures than in person. "Beginning at Moses and all the Prophets, He expounded to them in all the Scriptures the things concerning Himself." That way, every believer since has the same privilege they had.

After He broke bread with them and vanished, they "rose up that very hour" and went back to Jerusalem: fourteen miles in one day, over hilly ground. Where did the energy come from? From seeing Jesus in the Word. Ask Him to open your eyes every time you read, and expect it to strengthen you, body and soul.
